key_insight: Manifold-constrained hyper-connections can be understood geometrically on the Birkhoff polytope as a mean channel that behaves like a residual network plus a difference channel that decays at a rate set by the mixer’s second singular value.
engineering_relevance: This gives Transformer designers a principled way to predict how much extra width actually matters, and how Sinkhorn-based mixing and updates will behave during training and optimization.
method: Decompose doubly stochastic mixing into mean and difference channels.
Analyze Sinkhorn normalization as a global chart with Fisher-Rao geometry and entropic mirror descent.
Bound vertex approach/escape rates and Sinkhorn convergence using singular-value-based contraction.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experiments that confirm the predicted contraction, convergence, and rate laws.
watch_item: The practical benefit depends on Sinkhorn iteration budget and mixer conditioning, so limited normalization steps may weaken the intended long-horizon width effects.
paper_title: The Birkhoff Geometry of Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections: Two Channels, Vertex Viscosity, and Sinkhorn as a Retraction
